role: The append-only record of explicit OWNER RULINGS: decisions that dispose of a subject where no derivation could. A ruling is a decision with a name and a date on it, bound to exact paths and exact digests, and it is recorded here so that a DECIDED disposition can never be presented as a historically INFERRED one.
why: A derived ledger that quietly absorbs an owner decision launders a judgement into a derivation. Nine bound overlay members had no derivable disposition, and the honest state of each was a withheld attribution. The owner decided them. The decision is real, it is not a derivation, and the two must remain distinguishable by machine — otherwise the next reader cannot tell which of the 220 dispositions git could reproduce and which one a person chose.

rules.append_only: Rulings and the decisions inside them are appended and never rewritten or reordered. `sequence` is dense and starts at 1 in both dimensions; a gap is a removed decision and a repeat is a rewritten one.
rules.individual_not_family: A decision binds EXACTLY ONE path and EXACTLY ONE sha256. Nine decisions are nine records. A ruling may never be expressed as a directory rule, a glob, a programme-wide predicate, or a family rule, and tools/check-overlay-dispositions.mjs rejects a ruled member that any family rule enumerates.
rules.digest_bound: A decision names the digest the subject carried when it was decided. If the bytes move, the decision no longer applies to what is on disk and the member returns to a withheld attribution rather than inheriting a decision about different bytes.
rules.decision_source_is_load_bearing: Every disposition in program/canon-overlay-dispositions.v1.json carries `decision_source`. `derived` and `explicit_owner_ruling` are mutually exclusive, both directions are checked, and a mismatch in EITHER direction fails the bar.
rules.a_ruling_is_not_a_verification: Recording a ruling asserts that the owner decided. It asserts nothing about whether the ruled bytes are correct, current, or sufficient, verifies nothing, closes nothing, and discharges no hold.

decision_source_vocabulary.derived: The disposition was produced by an executable predicate over real bytes and real git facts, and re-running the derivation reproduces it byte-for-byte. Nobody chose it.
decision_source_vocabulary.explicit_owner_ruling: The disposition was CHOSEN by the owner, at named paths and named digests, because no derivation was available. Re-running the derivation reproduces it only because the derivation READS THIS LEDGER — never because the evidence implies it.

claim_boundary: A ruling records an owner decision at a moment, bound to exact bytes. It grants no coverage to any canon subject, admits no claim any ruled artifact makes, advances no baseline, certifies nothing, and discharges no hold.

rulings.title: Custody of the nine unattributed canon-overlay members
rulings.subject_summary: The nine bound canon-overlay members for which no tracked blob anywhere in this repository's history names the member by path, by basename, or by the schemaVersion its own bytes declare, and for which the derivation therefore withheld attribution.
rulings.decides: disposition = retained_nonclaim_evidence, custodian = m0-overlay-member-custody-and-disposition-successor, decision_source = explicit_owner_ruling, for each of nine individually-named path/digest pairs.
rulings.not_a_family_rule: These nine are NINE INDIVIDUAL CUSTODY DECISIONS. They are not a directory rule, not a programme rule, and not a family inference. They share a disposition and a custodian the way nine separate signatures can share a date; no one of them is evidence for another, and removing one changes nothing about the other eight.

binds_manifest.never_edited: The frozen v1 manifest is READ here and is not touched. A ruling about custody is not a change to the enumeration.

evidentiary_restriction.statement: The 'proven', 'final', 'verdict', 'complete', 'PASS' and equivalent language embedded in these nine artifacts is HISTORICAL ARTIFACT CONTENT. It is what the artifact said when it was written. It is NOT a claim this estate admits, and recording custody of the bytes adopts none of it.
evidentiary_restriction.permitted_uses_detail: They may be read, cited by path and digest, and used to investigate what was done and when. That is the whole of the permission.
evidentiary_restriction.prohibited_uses_detail: None of these nine artifacts may establish current product behaviour, architecture conformance, stage closure, compliance, performance, or any release claim. Not individually, not in aggregate, and not by being cited from a record that does make such a claim.
evidentiary_restriction.lifted_only_by: A SEPARATELY VERIFIED SUCCESSOR. The restriction is lifted for a specific assertion only when a successor record re-proves that assertion on its own evidence and reaches `verified` legitimately. Nothing about this ruling, this ledger, custody, retention, content addressing, or a promotion event lifts any part of it.
not_lifted_by: retention in place or in CAS
a promotion event admitting these bytes
the passing of any bar in this estate
evidentiary_restriction.machine_readable: This restriction is carried as a structured object on every one of the nine disposition entries, not only in prose, so a consumer can refuse a prohibited use without parsing English.

retention.rule: Retained in place under docs/evidence/ at the frozen digest recorded in each decision, and content-addressed under _archive/evidence/cas/. Never deleted, never rewritten, never cited as proof of anything.
retention.review_trigger: Re-decided when the named custody record reaches a terminal state, when any inbound citation appears, or when the bytes at a bound path stop carrying the bound digest.

decisions.binds_exactly_one_subject: ONE path and ONE digest. This decision is not a directory rule, not a family rule, not a predicate over siblings, and not an inference from the programme this file happens to sit under. Eight other decisions in this ruling look similar and none of them decides this one.
decisions.why_no_derivation_was_available: No tracked blob anywhere in this repository's history names this member — not by path, not by basename, and not by the schemaVersion its own bytes declare. The only remaining route to an owner would be the directory it sits in or the enumeration that lists it, and both are refused.
decisions.what_the_ruling_replaces: The withheld attribution. Before this ruling the member carried `unattributed` with the reason above. The ruling does not make the derivation succeed and does not claim a producer was found; it records that the OWNER decided custody where derivation could not.
